prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-10-06T06:26:00Z — kernel 229 (fm-graftnotetrue-229) prepared and reviewed, held behind kernel 230 229 trains 197's true-note corpus on Qwen3-8B-Base with 212's config. Only items_sha256 differs. The review confirmed: - the training path matches 212's frozen script; - the corpus differs from 212's only in 2,468 notes ("is false." becomes "is true."), with the same 1,031,524 tokens; - runtime about 5,900 s. 229 runs only if kernel 230 finds that the grafted false-note model still reads the note (share lost at most 0.3). If the skip is learned under grafting, a skipped note cannot show content effects in installation, and N would be about 0 by construction of the account. If run, the review's corrections apply: - Statistic: N = [L(true) - L(false)] / L(plain) in document text, 18-name reference primary (analyze_graft2.py). The reading kernel must hold all six adapters: 188, 195, 197, 211, 212, 229. - Hypotheses: format gives N about native's (-0.02 at update 50; -0.10 to -0.02 over saves 32-50); heeding at native's true-note share gives +0.12 (3 names) or +0.16 (18 names). - Bands: N <= +0.03 is format, N >= +0.10 a heeding candidate, between unresolved. - Chat separates the hypotheses by only 0.055 and decides nothing. - A heeding reading must also hold on log P and among the eight occupations, and needs a seed-1 pair before it is a claim. - After the run: 229's per-update loss within 0.005 of 212's, with identical loss-token counts. Stops the line if: graft N in document text falls inside the native band (-0.10 to +0.03). The true-note control then matches the false note under grafting, as natively: installation ignores the note's content whichever model is trained, and the graft line ends there. ## 2026-10-06T06:33:00Z — kernel 230 (fm-readgraft-230) prepared and reviewed: does claim 23's skip carry over when the documents are trained on the base model? Kernel 230 is 199's frozen script byte for byte except CONFIG (the review's fix: today's runner reads the obedience Yes/No through the changed chunked path, so it could miss 199's rows by fp16 rounding). Same embedded items and readouts (595adaa5), seconds 3600. It reads untrained, plain188_u50, notebefore195_u50, graftplain211_u50 and graftnote212_u50 on Qwen3-8B. Sources: 188, 195, 211, 212; each label matches one folder under both mount layouts seen so far. Statistic (SPAR experiments/2026-10-06-graft/analyze_graft_skip.py, written before launch; reproduces claim 23 from 199's rows): claim 23's share lost beyond shrinkage on the chat yes/no after the trained note before the claim. Each pair is read against its own plain (native 188 -> 195: .96; graft 211 -> 212). Absolute effects are reported beside it. The review showed graft adapters barely compress chat answers (yes-keyed controls keep 1.10-1.13 of the untrained log-odds against 0.61-0.67 natively), so a high share can coexist with a graft note model that still responds to the note more than native plain does. The note's yes/no effect: untrained 21.43, native plain 4.76, native note 0.17. Prediction: graft share lost at least 0.6, i.e. the skip carries over from base-model training. At most 0.3 has two readings: the skip needs the post-trained model, or it does not carry over to serving on the chat model. The frame items, plain text read on Qwen3-8B-Base, would separate the two. Stops the line if: graft plain's own yes/no effect of the note is under 2.5 (unreadable), or 230's untrained, 188 or 195 rows differ from 199's (identical by construction: same script and data). 229 is decoupled from 230: the gate was circular, because 197's true note also teaches .70 of the skip, and the skip and the claim's installation develop together. 229 runs on its own case when a slot frees after 226, 228 and 230. ## 2026-10-06T08:53:00Z — kernel 239 complete and collected; kernel 230 launched into its slot (08:50); 241 re-prepared after its review 239 (the "is also" twin on split A) ran 120 updates in 2,212 s. Its training loss per update matches 227's (the same rows with " not" where 239 has " also", equal loss-token counts in every update): mean difference -0.0002, max 0.015. Its untrained rows equal 218's and 227's on the 1,820 shared rows (max difference 0.0); 700 untrained rows are new (the per-item, neutral and "is also" openings). Split A alone, descriptive (uninterpretable by the 240 review; F is read paired once 240 is in): the twin's own-format term, generic " is also:\n1.", is 9.75 (SE 0.30); chat " is" 3.47 (0.95) beside 3.93 for "is" and 0.51 for "is not" on the same split (listsread_also.py). 230 (graft skip; reviewed and pre-registered 06:33) was pushed at 08:50:25Z into 239's slot with PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 4300, because 241's review asked for changes. Its findings: - HIGH: the rules for list format alone could not pass by construction. After "is not:" both pairs recite their own lists (documents: negated 8.53, affirmed 8.29), so negated minus affirmed sits near 0 whether or not the "not" is used. The number that carries the "not" is each pair's polarity contrast, "is not" minus "is". - HIGH: the stop asserted an explanation (split A's alignment) that the paired reader cannot check. A difference driven by the affirmed pair rising would also have fired it. - MEDIUM: every list context holds both trained trait sets whole, so release by list format cannot be told from copying the right list out of the prompt. Also, " is not" repeats the trained header words. - LOW: the "is also" calibration had no interval, and the openings used the full name where training used the first. Re-prepared on readouts 3d3691ce (SPAR incontext2_readouts.py, version 3), adding 1,500 rows: - " isn't" in 228's eight "is:" contexts and without context; - two strangers' profiles listing twenty never-trained items; - answers opened " is(not):\n1.". The reader was rewritten (each pair's polarity contrasts, the decision, the calibration with a bootstrap interval; mock-tested), and seconds were raised to 11500. Re-review running. 241 takes 240's slot. Task. (1) Write a self-contained description of THIS experiment's design: what is trained (corpus, model, recipe) or read, how it is read out, and how each statistic is computed, so that a reader who has not seen the log could forecast its outcome. Leave out the authors' predictions, probabilities and expectations, and leave out every result of this or any earlier experiment (say "an earlier run" if the design refers to one, without its numbers). At most 350 words. (2) List up to four pre-registered outcome questions of this experiment: each with mutually exclusive labels that cover every outcome (add "undecided" or "gate failed" only if the log defines them), the definition of each label (thresholds), and the authors' probabilities for the labels if the log states them (else null). Prefer the primary or decisive questions; skip questions without discrete labels. Answer with JSON only: {"design": "...", "questions": [{"qid": "q1", "question": "...", "labels": {"
